title: Piron's boat trips and sleeping quarters
summary: Furthest trip was St. Louis; slept below deck; summer season on the boat; about two years with Piron's band.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: I probably heard you with them maybe once or twice. Didn't know you in those days. To get back to Pierone's band, do you remember how far up the river you went?

Well, I didn't go no further than St. Louis with the band. St. Louis. That's the furthest I went with the band. But they had made trips all around Minneapolis. Yes, they went on Central, Minnesota. Well, I saw them advertising.
They went to Quixey, Illinois, or Kyrgyz, Iowa, or Hannibal, Missouri. That's right. I went on there. I went on by. Did you all sleep on the boat then?
Yeah, we slept on the boat down there in the bottom in the hall or something like that. That's where our sleeping quarters was.
Did you ever play on the boat when they got back to New Orleans here?
Yes, we stayed on the boat during the whole summer season mostly. Before Easter Monday, the boat would leave out.

But I wasn't fortunate enough to get that trip. I got it on the last when things was going down there. Because we played here one season, and that last season we were taking the boat up to St. Louis, and that was all.
Did you ever play any other jobs at Pierone around here?
Well, yes, I stayed with Pierone's band, I'd say about two years or better. 41. Yes.
What did he call it then?
A.J. Pierone. Yeah, that's right. Own name on the band.
